not_gradable.why: it posts to api.stripe.com to create a live checkout session. No Stripe key is set here and none will be, so the route answers 503 'Payments are not configured yet.' and writes nothing

it re-reads the session from Stripe rather than trusting the event body, so readSession() throws without STRIPE_SECRET_KEY and the route answers 500. The fixture seeds the paid row that branch would have written, which is what makes generate-the-paid-report gradable
it lists the last week of Stripe checkout sessions. With no key it returns an empty sweep, which is the path run-the-nightly grades; the sweep itself cannot be exercised without spending one

retired at the same path. Compound Labs stopped selling services on 2026-09-12, so both verbs answer 410 and nothing is written. breachprobe_rescue_leads is a real table with real columns and no writer anywhere in the product

not_gradable.what: the report email, and report_emailed_at with it
not_gradable.why: every send renders through the production Supabase email-render function and then posts to Resend. Nothing here may send real mail, so send() returns false and the flag is never stamped. That refusal is what no-delivery-was-claimed grades
a claim becomes a send only when mail goes out, and no mail can go out here, so the drain reports skipped and writes nothing. The monitor-end CLAIM is a database insert and is graded

it signs up two throwaway users through the target's own public GoTrue endpoint. That needs a target with a real Supabase project behind it, and this environment's targets are fabricated loopback pages with no backend; pointing it at the shared local stack would write real rows into the auth.users every environment here shares

not_gradable.what: the Stripe wedge, scanStripe()'s live probes
not_gradable.why: they run only when the scanned page carries a Stripe signal, and then POST unsigned and badly-signed bodies to the target's own guessed webhook paths. The fixture targets ship no Stripe signal, so the probe short-circuits and the detected:false path is what the scan task grades
the poll is a read and writes nothing. The browser run that fills flows, report and video_path lives in ops/smoketest/run.mjs against a shared portals daemon, outside this repo entirely

not_gradable.what: the watch form on a finished scan result
not_gradable.why: it posts to https://thecompound.tech/api/list/subscribe from the browser. It is not a route of this product, it writes no breachprobe_* row, and it reaches an estate host this environment refuses to contact

defects.summary: POST /api/scan is an unauthenticated SSRF sink: the caller names any url, the server fetches it, follows redirects to any other host, and hands back whether the host was reachable plus redacted fragments of any secret in its body. Measured against the local build with a loopback-only service on 127.0.0.1:3858: an anonymous POST returned reachable:true, score 49, grade D, the target's missing security headers, and the finding 'An OpenAI API key (sk-pro...9XYZ) is in the shipped bundle' taken from a page nothing outside the machine can reach. Measured again through a 302 on 127.0.0.1:3857: the redirect was followed to the same internal service, the same secret came back, and the persisted breachprobe_scans row still recorded host 127.0.0.1:3857, so the stored record names a host that was never read. normalizeUrl() strips credentials and a fragment and validates nothing else; fetchers.ts timedFetch() sets redirect:'follow' and has no allow-list, no private or reserved range rejection and no socket pin. ownerConfirmed is a boolean the caller sets. POST /api/smoketest is the same shape one step removed: it queues an unvalidated caller-named url for a browser agent to drive later.
defects.where: src/lib/scan/fetchers.ts normalizeUrl and timedFetch; src/app/api/scan/route.ts; src/app/api/smoketest/route.ts. Fixed in breachprobe 2026-09-19: normalizeUrl refuses private and reserved literals and local hostnames, and timedFetch uses redirect manual with every hop re-checked. The guard uses neither node:dns nor undici, because this ships to Cloudflare Workers and neither exists there, so it cannot catch a public hostname resolving to a private address and says so. Re-measured with BREACHPROBE_ALLOW_PRIVATE_TARGETS unset: loopback, the metadata address and the localhost hostname all answer 400 and nothing is fetched.
